***    *   *  *   *
 *   *   **  *   * * 
 *****   * * *    *  
 *   *   *  **    *

Any() Architecture Scanner

Same engine, two ways in:
  anyscan scan <path>   CLI (terminal, CI)
  anyscan mcp           MCP (Cursor). Tools: scan, list_rules, explain_rule

Usage:
  anyscan scan <path> [--depth surface|standard|deep] [--format text|json|sarif] [--output <file>] [--fail-on none|warning|error] [--include-tests] [--with-dotnet-analyzers]
  anyscan mcp

Reads anyarchitecture.json from the repository root when present.
MCP logs go to stderr. You do not need both; pick CLI or MCP.
A summary is printed first. In a terminal, anyscan then asks before writing a JSON file.
--output and --export write the report without asking. Progress is written to stderr.
--depth surface   file/project scanners only (secrets, production config, layers, BFF, CORS, health). Skips Roslyn.
--depth standard  surface plus Roslyn and the architecture graph. Default.
--depth deep      standard plus --include-tests and --with-dotnet-analyzers.
--include-tests also scans test projects for secrets and configuration issues
(skipped by default). Use this for an optional full scan in CI.
--with-dotnet-analyzers also runs the target solution's own configured CA/.NET
analyzers (via MSBuild) and folds their findings into the report. Any() does not
reimplement those checks; this just surfaces what the project already has enabled.
Slower than the default scan because it loads the solution through MSBuild.
Has no effect with --depth surface.
